answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to climb a reputation ridge before it can transact: each agent holds one cipher keypair whose history is public, and every completed job adds a small, decaying credit to a shared reef of attestations maintained by peers. New identities start with zero credit and must earn it through verifiable useful work, so creating thousands of sock puppets buys no spending power. Because credits decay when idle, a dormant army cannot be stockpiled for a later flood, and the cost of forging a credible history exceeds any gain from faking one.
